title: How do we construct a sixty degree angle with a compass?
description: A segment with its end marked, then two arcs of one radius that meet at a new point. Joining the three points gives a triangle with three equal sides, and its corner at the end of the segment is the angle we wanted. Keeko's doubt, a smaller radius for the second arc, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: two arcs of the same radius make an equilateral triangle, and each angle of it is sixty degrees. Watch for students who change the compass opening between the two arcs.

source: Construct a 60° angle at A on a segment AX using only a rule
video_script.why: The child sees that an equilateral triangle gives an exact sixty degree angle with no measuring.
video_script.substitution: The compass opening is kept fixed, so both arcs have the same radius.
video_script.anchor: A segment AX with the point A marked, a ruler and a compass.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws the second arc from B with a smaller radius. Then BC is shorter than AB, the triangle is not equilateral, and the angle is not sixty degrees.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle C eigh X is sixty degrees.

final_answer.spoken: angle C eigh X is sixty degrees

maths_rules: AB = AC, because both are radii of the first arc.
BA = BC, because both are radii of the second arc, which has the same radius.
So AB = BC = CA and triangle ABC is equilateral.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so ∠CAX = 60°.
Slip: a smaller radius from B makes BC shorter than AB, so the triangle is not equilateral.
video_script.design: One segment, one compass opening, two arcs and a triangle with three equal sides. The sides are drawn equal only because they are radii. The slip is a smaller second arc.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the second arc from B can use a smaller radius.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then B C would be shorter than eigh B, so the three sides would not be equal.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The triangle would not be equilateral, and the angle would not be sixty degrees. The compass must keep the same opening for both arcs.
